svg.title: Copper Scroll entry 35: Kidron: the cairn at the mouth of the gorge
svg.text: Entry 35 (VIII 8–9) — Kidron: the cairn at the mouth of the gorge
Schematic plan, north up; the valley runs west to east, as the Kidron does. One arrangement the text allows; not a map of the real gorge.
Project reading: a cairn where the valley enters the Kidron gorge
Milik and Puech: a heap of stones beside the path, at the gorge reached from Jerusalem before
Mar Saba. The text gives no distance from anything; only the depth, three cubits.
flow east, to the Dead Sea
a heap of stones (Milik, Puech, Høgenhaven)
mouth of the gorge · פי צוק
Wolters, Pixner read “pottery” for the name; the plan is the same.
SECTION at the cairn · depth to scale
from the ground at the cairn
Luria, Eshel 2002: a dam, not a cairn
Eshel: the dam where Hyrcania's southern aqueduct began
Not adopted · Puech rejects the dam
Lefkovits 2000: a peak, not a gorge
צוק read as “peak” (p. 262), a different landmark.
The files give no placement for this reading.
The gorge near Mar Saba (Milik, Puech), or where the Kidron
leaves the escarpment (Dahari)? The files leave it open.
“In the cairn at the mouth of the Kidron gorge, dig three cubits: 7 talents.”
A heap of stones beside the path where the open valley enters the gorge, reached from Jerusalem
(Milik, Puech). The dig starts at the cairn; its level is not stated. Sum 7 as Puech and Lefkovits
Best-supported, medium: Kidron gorge (Wadi en-Nar) at Deir Mar Saba, exact stretch unresolved.
Hyrcania (Kh. el-Mird) possible, low: the link rests on restorations and the “dam” reading.
SWP III shows the open valley and the gorge by Mar Saba, but no source consulted records a cairn
there; the Kidron is also a canyon where it leaves the escarpment (Dahari), so “the mouth of the
gorge” does not fix the Mar Saba end (phase5_assessments.csv).
